title: Color and energy
hook: Explore the evidence behind a cosmic question.

knows: Light and gravity help astronomers study the universe.
doesNotKnow: A photon's energy is proportional to its frequency. Higher-frequency electromagnetic radiation has more energy per photon than lower-frequency radiation.

misconception: A learner may choose: It decreases
objective: Use the visual model to reason about: How does the energy of a photon change when its frequency increases?

claims.text: Question, correct answer and explanation: How does the energy of a photon change when its frequency increases? It increases. A photon's energy is proportional to its frequency. Higher-frequency electromagnetic radiation has more energy per photon than lower-frequency radiation.
Visual caption: Higher frequency, more energy. The SVG is a conceptual illustration, not measured data or a scale model.

recall.question: How does the energy of a photon change when its frequency increases?
recall.why: A photon's energy is proportional to its frequency. Higher-frequency electromagnetic radiation has more energy per photon than lower-frequency radiation.
